title: Don't be fooled: that viral Texas Tech fan taking social media by storm is pure AI
key_facts: An image of a supposed Texas Tech fan watching the Red Raiders play Houston drew wide attention online.
The image reportedly generated around 10 million views; one post had more than 38,000 likes and about 9.6 million views.
According to The Spun, the picture was most likely created with AI rather than taken at the game.
MARCA contrasts it with a real viral fan, Sara Smith of Ole Miss, shown on ESPN during a 41-38 win over Louisville in September.
MARCA says fact-checkers documented AI-made images of unusual spectators and public figures during the 2026 FIFA World Cup, some with millions of views.
quote_evidence: There is one major problem with the viral moment, however: the fan featured in the circulating image is not real.
According to reporting by The Spun, the picture was most likely created using artificial intelligence rather than captured during the actual college football game.
The image reportedly generated around 10 million views, with one post receiving more than 38,000 likes and approximately 9.6 million views.
why_it_matters_hint: A convincing fake sports fan went viral, showing how hard it is to tell real from AI images at live events.
event_date: Not stated (game and posts around 10 to 11 Oct 2026)
notes: MARCA relays The Spun, which was not opened here; source credited to The Spun, with MARCA named in the summary. The finding is "most likely", not proven.
